stem: A hospital quality team reviews a Medicare IPPS case in which a Stage III pressure injury developed during the hospitalization and was not present on admission. Which CMS payment principle applies under the Hospital-Acquired Conditions Present-on-Admission payment provision?

options.A: The hospital does not receive additional payment attributable to the selected HAC; the case is paid as though that secondary diagnosis were not present
options.B: Every occurrence automatically causes a 1% reduction in all Medicare payments to the hospital for the year
options.C: The hospital receives a higher DRG payment because the new pressure injury increases case severity
options.D: The condition is excluded from HAC policy because pressure injuries are not on the CMS HAC list

rationale: CMS states that for selected Hospital-Acquired Conditions that were not present on admission, the hospital does not receive additional payment attributable to that condition; the case is paid as though the secondary diagnosis were not present. Stage III and IV pressure ulcers are included on the HAC list. This HAC Present-on-Admission payment provision is separate from the HAC Reduction Program, which can reduce payments by 1% for hospitals in the worst-performing quartile on selected HAC measures. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Distinguish the CMS HAC Present-on-Admission payment provision from the separate HAC Reduction Program and recognize the payment implication of a selected HAC that was not present on admission.
source_document_title: Hospital-Acquired Conditions — Present on Admission Indicator and HAC Payment Provision
source_locator: Sections 'Present on Admission Indicator' and 'HAC Payment Provision': selected conditions are high cost/high volume, result in higher DRG payment as secondary diagnoses, and could reasonably have been prevented; for selected HACs not present on admission, hospitals do not receive additional payment and the case is paid as though the secondary diagnosis were not present; HAC list includes Stage III and IV Pressure Ulcers
source_claim_supported: For a selected HAC such as a Stage III/IV pressure ulcer that was not present on admission, the HAC POA payment provision prevents additional payment attributable to that secondary diagnosis.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22 / PDF p.26: participate in performance-improvement projects and quality-improvement processes; evaluate impact of performance-improvement measures on client care and resource use; practice and advocate for quality and cost-effective care
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement / CMS HAC-POA payment provision
correction_summary: Corrected a substantive program mismatch. The source item attributed the no-additional-payment rule to the HAC Reduction Program, but CMS identifies it as the separate HAC Present-on-Admission payment provision. Rewrote the item to test the exact current payment rule and explicitly distinguish it from HACRP.
audit_findings: A exactly matches CMS's current HAC POA payment provision. B describes the distinct HAC Reduction Program's 1% penalty in an overgeneralized way and is not triggered by a single case. C is the opposite of the HAC payment rule. D is false because Stage III/IV pressure ulcers are listed HACs. The IPPS context is explicit because the payment provision applies to IPPS hospitals. One best answer remains; NCSBN Performance Improvement/resource-use mapping is appropriate. Independent second pass found no unresolved policy conflict.

final_reaudit_scope: current CMS HAC POA versus HACRP distinction; exact CMS locator; claim-by-claim; A-D distractor audit; ambiguity/second-answer/cueing; NCSBN 2026 blueprint; independent adversarial second pass
